title: Firestore TTL / retention policy manifest
description: Declarative source of truth for which Firestore collections hold unbounded or time-series data and therefore MUST have a retention policy (a `ttl:true` field override + a live GCP TTL policy, or an explicit compaction plan). This manifest declares INTENT: enabling a live TTL policy in Google Cloud is an operator action (see operatorAction). scripts/ci/check-firestore-ttl-declared.sh fails closed when firestore.indexes.json declares a `ttl:true` field for a collection that is not registered here, or when a policy's `indexDeclared` claim disagrees with firestore.indexes.json. Live-state readback lives in scripts/ci/verify-firestore-ttl-state.mjs and scripts/security/verify-deployed-ttl.sh (both need gcloud). Cost impact of each unbounded collection is modelled in docs/ops/UNIT_ECONOMICS_COST_MODEL.md.

conventions.collectionGroup: Firestore collection-group id (the last path segment). TTL policies in GCP are keyed by collection-group + field, so nested collections that share a name (e.g. `providers` under both a day bucket and the all_time bucket) share one TTL policy.
conventions.mechanism: firestore-ttl-field = a `ttl:true` override on ttlField deletes each doc after its stamped `expireAt`/`expiresAt`. aggregate-compaction = growth is inside a document (map/array field), not a doc count, so a field TTL cannot prune it; needs a scheduled compaction/rollover. recursive-delete = pruned by a scheduled function, not GCP TTL.
conventions.indexDeclared: true iff firestore.indexes.json currently carries a `ttl:true` fieldOverride for {collectionGroup, ttlField}. The check enforces this matches reality in both directions.
conventions.status: active = TTL field is declared in firestore.indexes.json and expected live in GCP (proven by verify-firestore-ttl-state.mjs). pending-operator-enablement = retention intent is declared here but NOT yet wired; an operator still has to act.
conventions.retentionSeconds: Intended maximum age before deletion. null when retention is per-window/variable or handled by compaction rather than a single age.

policies.growth: One document per active user per day, retained forever today.
policies.retention: 400 days (intent; operator to confirm against paid-tier history window)
policies.operatorAction: 1) stamp `expireAt = createdDay + retention` when writing day docs in functions/src/rollupCounters.ts; 2) add {collectionGroup: usage_counter_days, fieldPath: expireAt, ttl: true} to firestore.indexes.json and flip indexDeclared→true, status→active; 3) `gcloud firestore fields ttls update expireAt --collection-group=usage_counter_days --enable-ttl --project=burnbar`.
policies.rationale: functions/src/rollupCompute.ts documents that day docs are never deleted, so the scan grows with account age; TECH_DEBT_AUDIT_2026-06-11 #151 flags usage/usage_counter_keys/usage_counter_days as forever-growing with no compaction/archival story.

policies.growth: One document per (day x provider) per active user, retained forever today.
policies.ttlSafetyNote: The `providers` collection-group ALSO exists under users/{uid}/usage_counter_totals/all_time, which is bounded and must NOT be pruned. Because GCP TTL only deletes docs whose ttlField is a past timestamp, stamp `expireAt` ONLY on the per-day sub-counter docs and never on the all_time sub-counters.
policies.operatorAction: Stamp `expireAt` on the per-day `providers` sub-counter in functions/src/rollupCounters.ts (addContributionToBucket), then declare + enable TTL on collection-group `providers` as for usage_counter_days.
policies.rationale: Per-day provider sub-counters written alongside each day bucket grow one-per-provider-per-day forever.

policies.growth: One document per (day x account) per active user, retained forever today.
policies.ttlSafetyNote: Shared with the bounded all_time bucket; stamp `expireAt` only on the per-day `accounts` sub-counter docs.
policies.operatorAction: Stamp `expireAt` on the per-day `accounts` sub-counter, then declare + enable TTL on collection-group `accounts`.
policies.rationale: Per-day account sub-counters grow one-per-account-per-day forever.

policies.growth: One document per (day x provider:model) per active user, retained forever today.
policies.ttlSafetyNote: Shared with the bounded all_time bucket; stamp `expireAt` only on the per-day `models` sub-counter docs.
policies.operatorAction: Stamp `expireAt` on the per-day `models` sub-counter, then declare + enable TTL on collection-group `models`.
policies.rationale: Per-day model sub-counters grow one-per-model-per-day forever.

policies.growth: One document per (day x device) per active user, retained forever today.
policies.ttlSafetyNote: Shared with the bounded all_time bucket; stamp `expireAt` only on the per-day `devices` sub-counter docs.
policies.operatorAction: Stamp `expireAt` on the per-day `devices` sub-counter, then declare + enable TTL on collection-group `devices`.
policies.rationale: Per-day device sub-counters grow one-per-device-per-day forever.

policies.growth: Bounded to one `all_time` doc per user, BUT its `dailyTokens` map gains one key per active day forever.
policies.retention: n/a — a document-field TTL cannot prune an in-document map; needs compaction/rollover.
policies.operatorAction: Cap or roll over the `dailyTokens` map (e.g. keep a trailing window and fold older days into a scalar) in functions/src/rollupCounters.ts; GCP TTL does not apply.
policies.rationale: rollupCounters.ts grows the all_time `dailyTokens` map one key per active day so all_time rollups avoid rescanning usage_counter_days; unbounded map growth is a per-document cost, not a doc-count cost.

policies.growth: One document per outbound VoIP push, self-expiring.
policies.rationale: Ephemeral push-delivery docs carry uid + push tokens; F-RR09-001 requires they self-expire.

policies.growth: One document per outbound FCM push, self-expiring.
policies.rationale: Ephemeral push-delivery docs carry uid + push tokens; F-RR09-001 requires they self-expire.

policies.growth: One document per inbound call setup, self-expiring.
policies.rationale: Owner-scoped, TTL-bound call context used to resolve the active connection; must self-expire.

policies.growth: One document per agent notification event, self-expiring.
policies.rationale: Ephemeral notification events carry identifying metadata; F-RR09-007 requires bounded retention.

policies.growth: One document per processed Stripe webhook (idempotency ledger).
policies.rationale: LB-5: idempotency ledger kept long enough to defeat replayed webhooks, then aged out.

policies.growth: One document per credential transfer handshake, self-expiring.
policies.rationale: Short-lived credential handoff; must not linger.

policies.growth: One document per gateway device session, self-expiring.
policies.rationale: Short gateway session lease; self-expires so stale sessions do not accumulate.

policies.growth: One document per proof-of-possession nonce (anti-replay), self-expiring.
policies.rationale: Replay-guard nonces are only useful within the clock-skew window; must self-expire.

policies.growth: One document per rate-limit window (per action/day/month), self-expiring.
policies.retention: per-window (daily/monthly quota keys); each doc stamps its own expireAt
policies.rationale: Sliding-window rate-limit counters must age out with their window instead of accumulating.

policies.growth: One privacy-safe sample per eligible shared-Rust quota shadow comparison.
policies.operatorAction: Enable and verify live TTL with scripts/ci/verify-firestore-ttl-state.mjs before beta collection begins.
policies.rationale: Promotion evidence needs a bounded observation window and contains no uid, payload, parsed value, path, or stable device identifier.
